stem: During a prescriber call, a DEA registrant proposes discarding controlled-substance inventory records after 18 months. What is the minimum federal approach?

choices.text: Eighteen months is sufficient if records are scanned.
Retain only the most recent biennial inventory.
Use the five-year Massachusetts serious-event period for all DEA records.
Send records to DEA after one year and delete the pharmacy copies.
Maintain the DEA-required records for at least two years and keep them available for inspection.

explanation.core_reasoning: 'Maintain the DEA-required records for at least two years and keep them available for inspection.' is the governing result. By contrast, 'Eighteen months is sufficient if records are scanned.' would require that electronic format shortened the federal retention period. The decisive cue appears in 'During a prescriber call, a DEA registrant proposes discarding controlled-substance inventory records after 18 months. What is the minimum federal approach?'.

choice_analysis.A: 'Eighteen months is sufficient if records are scanned.' would apply only if electronic format shortened the federal retention period; 'During a prescriber call, a DEA registrant proposes discarding controlled-substance inventory records after 18 months. What is the minimum federal approach?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.B: 'Retain only the most recent biennial inventory.' would apply only if new inventories allowed destruction of still-required older records; 'During a prescriber call, a DEA registrant proposes discarding controlled-substance inventory records after 18 months. What is the minimum federal approach?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.C: 'Use the five-year Massachusetts serious-event period for all DEA records.' would apply only if the special state event-record rule set the federal minimum for every controlled record; 'During a prescriber call, a DEA registrant proposes discarding controlled-substance inventory records after 18 months. What is the minimum federal approach?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.D: 'Send records to DEA after one year and delete the pharmacy copies.' would apply only if transmission to DEA ended the registrant's availability obligation; 'During a prescriber call, a DEA registrant proposes discarding controlled-substance inventory records after 18 months. What is the minimum federal approach?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.E: 'Maintain the DEA-required records for at least two years and keep them available for inspection.': supported by retention.

related_facts: DEA-required controlled-substance inventories and records must be maintained and available for inspection for at least two years unless another provision requires longer.
